label: Taxe carbone mondiale à 150 $/tonne d'ici 6 ans

sources: IPCC AR6 WGIII Ch.13 — Carbon pricing reduces emissions across all sectors; $135–5500/tCO2 range covers 1.5°C trajectories
IMF 2021 — A universal $75/tCO2 tax could reduce global emissions ~35% by 2030; $150/tCO2 achieves deeper cuts
World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard 2024 — Over 20% of global GHG emissions covered by carbon pricing instruments
IPCC AR6 SYR SPM — Carbon pricing is one of the most economically efficient cross-sectoral policy instruments

societal_indicators.note: Higher energy costs may affect affordability without redistribution mechanisms
Regressive without revenue recycling; progressive with 60% redistribution to developing nations

interactions.note: Carbon price accelerates renewable deployment by making fossil alternatives more expensive
Both target fossil fuel phase-out; combined effect exceeds sum of parts
Carbon price raises relative cost of fossil vehicles, accelerating EV transition

methodological_note: A global $150/tCO2 carbon tax sits at the low end of IPCC AR6's $135–$5500/tCO2 range for 1.5°C trajectories (WGIII Ch.13.7). Median impact calibrated at 6 GtCO2/yr at full effect (~2050), consistent with cross-sector price elasticities and IMF modelling. Optimistic scenario assumes rapid behavioral change and complementary policies. Pessimistic scenario reflects incomplete global uptake and exemptions in industrial sectors. Projection baseline: SSP2-4.5 (37.4 GtCO2/yr in 2024, rising to 63.0 by 2074). Forest projections show modest improvement due to carbon pricing raising the opportunity cost of deforestation.
